questions.explanation: After fronted negative 'never' the auxiliary inverts with the subject for rhetorical emphasis.
questions.q: Choose the correctly inverted rhetorical form.

questions.explanation: 'Not only' at the front triggers inversion in the first clause; the second clause stays normal.
options: Not only did he resign, but he also sued
Not only he resigned, but also he sued
Not only did he resign, but also did he sue
Not only resigned he, but he also sued

questions.explanation: 'Rarely' is a negative adverbial that forces subject–auxiliary inversion when fronted.
'Little did' inverts the auxiliary and subject to express dramatic surprise.
questions.q: ___ what fate had in store for him.

questions.explanation: Fronted 'only after' triggers inversion in the clause it introduces.
options: Only after the trial did the truth emerge
Only after the trial the truth emerged
Only after the trial emerged the truth
Only after the trial did emerge the truth

questions.explanation: 'Under no circumstances' is a negative phrase requiring inversion of auxiliary and subject.
options: under no circumstances may you to

questions.explanation: 'So great' fronted for emphasis inverts the auxiliary before the subject.
'No sooner' requires inversion in its own clause, followed by 'than' in the second.
options: No sooner the bell rang than
No sooner rang the bell than
No sooner did the bell rang than
No sooner had the bell rung than

questions.explanation: 'Had' inverts with the subject in formal conditional clauses without 'if'.
questions.q: ___ the risks, I would never have agreed.

questions.explanation: 'Hardly' fronted triggers inversion and pairs with 'when', not 'than'.
'Seldom' is a negative frequency adverb that inverts when fronted for rhetoric.
questions.q: ___ an audience to tears as hers did.

questions.explanation: 'Were' inverts with the subject in formal hypothetical conditionals without 'if'.
'Not until' fronted inverts the clause it introduces for dramatic effect.
options: Not until dawn did they rest
Not until dawn did they rested

questions.explanation: In the main clause of a wish about the past, inversion follows 'never' with the past perfect auxiliary.
'Only by' fronted requires inversion in the following clause.
options: Only by protest the workers won
Only by protest did the workers win
Only by protest won the workers
Only by protest the workers did win

questions.explanation: 'Such' fronted with 'was' inverts subject and verb for rhetorical emphasis.
'Should' inverts with the subject in formal conditionals expressing unlikely futures.
questions.q: ___ assistance, do not hesitate to call.

questions.explanation: 'Scarcely' inverts the auxiliary and pairs with 'when' in formal narrative.
options: Scarcely did the ink dry than
Scarcely had the ink dried when
Scarcely had dried the ink when

questions.explanation: Fronted 'nowhere' is a negative adverbial forcing inversion of auxiliary and subject.
'In no way' fronted inverts the modal and subject for emphatic denial.
options: In no way am I being
In no way do I am
